text: APIs, or Application Programming Interfaces, allow different software systems to talk to each other. When you work with an API, you typically send HTTP requests to a server to get or send data. Most modern APIs use JSON, a simple text format, to structure that data. Before you can use many APIs, you need to provide authentication, often using an API key, to prove who you are. Also, be aware of rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain time period. Finally, good error handling is crucial. You should always check the response status codes and build your code to deal with problems like network failures or invalid data.
